shared_elements: worked rectangular stone surface with carved decoration
horizontal band of repeated small marks/units running across the upper area
rows of repeated units arranged in registers
vertical border strips filled with repeated marks along the edges
justification: Both are upright tan stone surfaces organised into registers, and each carries a horizontal band of repeated small units near the top plus repeated marks running down the vertical edges, which is the most specific correspondence. Otherwise they diverge completely: A is a flat slab with thin, shallow incised straight lines and abstract sign-like characters, while B is a thick pillar carved in bold raised relief with recognisable animals (long-necked birds, quadrupeds) and no comparable linear script-like content.
